title: Make public discovery listing time filters respect event wall-clock storage
detail: Latest checked-in public_events(integer) function compares e.starts_at >= now() directly even though event starts_at stores host wall-clock parts as UTC. For Pacific 19:00 stored as 19:00Z, at 17:00 Pacific (00:00Z next day) the event is filtered from discovery before it begins. The RPC also omits time_zone, so downstream city filtering cannot resolve non-home event zones. SCAN-1036 repairs the independent public share page and sitemap end checks using existing zone reads, but cannot recover rows already discarded by this SQL listing filter. Trace matching calendar/listing RPCs and community-day floors, define intended in-progress policy, then prepare a migration with unchanged publication/visibility/Space-wall/demo/privacy gates and bounded ordering/limit behavior. No live event rows read or changed; source-confirmed consequence, not production impact proof. Applying shared schema changes requires explicit human authorization.

verify.evidence: Open: disposable SQL or authorized staging proof must retain Pacific events before their true start, exclude past events according to the chosen policy, cover London/Auckland and DST boundaries, preserve all visibility/privacy gates and demonstrate downstream timezone projection. No migration applied.
